themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.0 per week, a 500% increase (z-score: 5.0), signaling an acute sanitation failure affecting residential waste pickup in Mott Haven/Melrose.
evidence: 6 Missed Collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Complaint type ranks as statistically significant anomaly (severity: high)
Converges with Street Sweeping spike (11 complaints last week vs 1.6 avg) suggesting broader sanitation infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if this week's spike reflects route changes, staffing shortages, or equipment failures
Interview residents about visible garbage accumulation and health/rodent concerns in the past 7 days
Check if missed collections are clustered geographically (specific blocks) or citywide

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For Hire Vehicle complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 1.1 per week, a 256% increase (z-score: 3.68), indicating a potential surge in unlicensed or improperly operated rideshare activity.
evidence: 4 For Hire Vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (256% spike, z-score: 3.68)
Complaint type classified as high-severity statistical anomaly
Suggests potential enforcement gap or new illicit rideshare operations in the district
reporting_angles: Interview TLC (Taxi and Limousine Commission) about enforcement activity in CD 201 this week
Survey residents and businesses about unsafe driving, congestion, or unlicensed vehicle activity observed recently
Map complaint locations to identify if spike is concentrated near transit hubs (subway stations, major avenues)

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaint Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis Retailer complaints reached 4 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week, a 1500% increase (z-score: 8.66, highest severity), indicating rapid illegal or unauthorized cannabis shop activity or community backlash against new legal retail.
evidence: 4 Cannabis Retailer complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66, highest z-score in dataset)
Largest statistical anomaly in the full complaint dataset this period
Suggests either proliferation of unlicensed dispensaries or organized community objection to licensed retail opening
reporting_angles: Identify which cannabis retailers (licensed or unlicensed) opened or expanded in CD 201 in the past 2 weeks; cross-check with NY State OCM (Office of Cannabis Management) licensed retailer database
Interview community board members, local business owners, and residents about their concerns—odor, loitering, youth access, or quality-of-life impacts
Determine if complaints are concentrated near schools or residential blocks, and whether enforcement (NYPD, State Police) is active

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Street Sweeping complaints jumped to 11 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.6 per week, a 577% increase (z-score: 6.27), indicating widespread neglect of street cleanliness and sidewalk maintenance across the district.
evidence: 11 Street Sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (577% spike, z-score: 6.27)
Converges with Missed Collection spike THIS WEEK (6 vs 1.0 avg), suggesting systemic sanitation breakdown
Community Board has requested street signage/wayfinding for years, indicating chronic infrastructure neglect in district
reporting_angles: Request DSNY sweeping schedules and actual completion logs for CD 201 blocks to identify gaps
Walk major streets (Grand Concourse, East 138th, East 149th) and photograph visible debris, trash accumulation
Interview residents about timeline—did street conditions deteriorate suddenly last week, or is this chronic?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints reached 10 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 2.2 per week, a 344% increase (z-score: 3.91), marking a sharp rise in homeless encampments or visible street homelessness in Mott Haven/Melrose.
evidence: 10 Encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (344% spike, z-score: 3.91)
Community Board has filed budget requests for homeless services for years (unsolved, recurring need)
Suggests either new encampments established last week or intensified resident reporting of existing ones
reporting_angles: Locate the specific blocks/parks where encampments are visible; map against DHS shelter capacity and street outreach resources in the district
Interview residents and local business owners about safety concerns, sanitation, and any incidents
Contact DHS and NYC Street Outreach Unit to determine if encampment count has actually risen or if reporting surged; identify barriers to shelter access
